16: /// ## Why is this bad?

20: /// ## Known problems
21: /// Prone to false positives when checking comments that resemble Python code,
22: /// but are not actually Python code ([#4845]).

52:     locator: &Locator,
53:     comment_ranges: &CommentRanges,
54:     settings: &LinterSettings,
55: ) {
56:     let mut comments = comment_ranges.into_iter().peekable();
57:     // Iterate over all comments in the document.
58:     while let Some(range) = comments.next() {

72:         }

75:         if is_own_line_comment(line) && comment_contains_code(line, &settings.task_tags[..]) {

85: struct ScriptTagScanner {

90: impl ScriptTagScanner {
91:     /// Parses the rest of a [PEP 723](https://peps.python.org/pep-0723/)
92:     /// script comment and moves `comments` past the script comment's end unless
93:     /// the script comment is invalid.
94:     ///
95:     /// Returns `true` if it is a valid script comment.
96:     fn skip_script_comments<I>(
97:         &mut self,
98:         comments: &mut std::iter::Peekable<I>,
99:         cursor: &mut ScriptTagCursor<'_>,
100:     ) -> bool
101:     where
102:         I: Iterator<Item = TextRange>,
103:     {
104:         while !cursor.text.is_empty() && cursor.offset < cursor.offset_back {
105:             cursor.line_start = cursor.offset;
106:             let remaining = cursor.text;
107:             let (line_with_ending, rest, ending_len) =
108:                 if let Some(position) = remaining.find(['\n', '\r']) {
109:                     let ending_len = if remaining.as_bytes()[position] == b'\r'
110:                         && remaining.as_bytes().get(position + 1) == Some(&b'\n')
111:                     {
112:                         2
113:                     } else {
114:                         1
115:                     };
116:                     let (line_with_ending, rest) = remaining.split_at(position + ending_len);
117:                     (line_with_ending, rest, ending_len)
118:                 } else {
119:                     (remaining, "", 0)
120:                 };
121:             cursor.text = rest;
122:             cursor.line_end = cursor.line_start + line_with_ending.text_len();
123:             cursor.offset = cursor.line_end;
124: 
125:             let line = &line_with_ending[..line_with_ending.len() - ending_len];
126:             let Some(content) = script_tag_line_body(line) else {
127:                 break;
128:             };
129: 
130:             if content == "///" {
131:                 // > Precedence for an ending line # /// is given when the next line is not a valid
132:                 // > embedded content line as described above.
133:                 // > For example, the following is a single fully valid block:
134:                 // > ```python
135:                 // > # /// some-toml
136:                 // > # embedded-csharp = """
137:                 // > # /// <summary>
138:                 // > # /// text
139:                 // > # ///
140:                 // > # /// </summary>
141:                 // > # public class MyClass { }
142:                 // > # """
143:                 // > # ///
144:                 // ````
145:                 let terminator = cursor.line_end;
146:                 if next_line_is_script_tag(cursor) {
147:                     continue;
148:                 }
149:                 self.terminator = Some(terminator);
150:                 break;
151:             }
152:         }
153: 
154:         // > Unclosed blocks MUST be ignored.
155:         let Some(end_offset) = self.terminator else {
156:             return false;
157:         };
158: 
159:         // Skip over all script-comments.
160:         while let Some(comment) = comments.peek() {
161:             if comment.start() >= end_offset || comment.start() < self.script_start.start() {
162:                 break;
163:             }
164: 
165:             comments.next();
166:         }
167: 
168:         true
169:     }
170: }

173:     if cursor.text.is_empty() || cursor.offset >= cursor.offset_back {
174:         return false;
175:     }
176: 
177:     cursor.line_start = cursor.offset;

193:     cursor.text = rest;

195:     cursor.offset = cursor.line_end;

part.text:
Fixed ERA001 false positives in PEP 723 inline script blocks with trailing comments.

The scanner now tracks the last `# ///` terminator while scanning the contiguous script block, so trailing comments after the closing tag no longer prevent the block from being recognized.

Validated with:
- `cargo test -q -p ruff_linter --lib` — 2219 passed
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`
- The reported example now passes `ruff check --select ERA001` cleanly.
